title: Correcting a Settled Rider Claim Line by Reversal
content:
A claim line already processed under one of the Optional Supplemental Benefit Riders is corrected by reversing that exact line and posting a corrected line in its place, never by editing the line that is already there.

## The line being reversed

The reversal names the single processed rider claim line it applies to, and that line is on record with a claim status of paid, denied or adjusted. This is read before the reversal is posted, from the member's own rider benefit claim history: the reference of the line, the line each entry names as the one it applies to, and the standing of each line.

## No reversal posted twice

No reversal of that same processed rider claim line is already on record. This too is judged before posting, on the member's rider benefit claim history — the references, the line each entry names as its subject and what kind of entry each is. Two reversals of one line differing only in the day they were processed are not thereby made separate.

## What the reversal carries

The reversal carries the negative of what the reversed line paid, so the benefit year maximum, the combined cap and the frequency counts all return to what they were before it.

## A correction following an appeal

Where the correction follows a successful appeal the corrected line is processed on the terms the appeal decision directs, and any amount the member already paid the provider above their proper share is refunded to the member.

## Recovering an overpayment

Money the rider overpaid a network provider is recovered from that provider and never taken from the member's next benefit.

## One line at a time

Each line is reversed on its own reference: a claim covering several teeth or both eyes is never reversed as a whole, because the lines may be settled differently.

## Points of judgement

**A denied line may be reversed.** The three standings on which a processed line may be reversed are paid, denied and adjusted; a line that is itself a reversal is not among them.

**The reversal restores three counts at once.** Because it carries the negative of what the reversed line paid, the benefit year maximum, the combined cap and the frequency counts all return to what they were.

**The member is not the source of the recovery.** Money the rider overpaid a network provider is recovered from that provider.
